name: Spades Partnership
description: Spades Partnership (often just 'Partnership Spades' or 'Cutthroat Spades' depending on context) refers to specific variations of Spades that emphasize the partnership aspect or introduce specific bidding constraints like 'Suicide' (one partner must bid Nil), 'Mirrors' (bid exactly your Spades), or 'Whiz' (Nil or Spades). It is played with the standard 4-player setup but with modified bidding rules.

overview.description: Spades Partnership (often just 'Partnership Spades' or 'Cutthroat Spades' depending on context) refers to specific variations of Spades that emphasize the partnership aspect or introduce specific bidding constraints like 'Suicide' (one partner must bid Nil), 'Mirrors' (bid exactly your Spades), or 'Whiz' (Nil or Spades). It is played with the standard 4-player setup but with modified bidding rules.

history.origins: Variations emerged as Spades became a household game. 'Suicide' became popular in college dorms to force action.
timeline: Present: Online platforms offer these as standard modes.
history.cultural: Often played when standard Spades feels too predictable.
history.evolution: These variations increase the tension by removing safe '2' or '3' bids.

setup.deck: A standard pack of 52 cards is used. The cards in each suit rank from highest to lowest: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2. Spades Partnership uses the same deck as basic Spades.
setup.dealing: The first dealer is chosen at random; the turn to deal rotates clockwise. The cards are shuffled and dealt singly, clockwise, beginning with the player on the dealer's left, until all 52 cards have been dealt and each player has 13 cards.

rules.objective: Each partnership aims to reach 500 points first by making at least the number of tricks it bid each hand. Teams score 10 points per trick bid when made; overtricks (bags) score 1 each with a 100-point penalty per 10 bags. Nil bids earn a bonus or penalty. Variants (Suicide, Mirrors, Whiz) impose stricter bidding rules but the same scoring goal.
rules.gameplay: Four players in fixed partnerships. Deal 13 cards each, one at a time, clockwise from left of dealer. Each player bids 0 to 13 tricks (Nil = 0); partnership bids are summed. Play 13 tricks: left of dealer leads; must follow suit if able; spades are always trump. Trick won by highest trump if any, else highest card of led suit. Winner of trick leads next. Spades may not be led until broken (a spade has been played on another suit) or leader has only spades. Score 10 per trick bid if made; overtricks (bags) score 1 each; 10 bags deduct 100. Nil: +100 if no tricks taken, -100 if any trick taken. First side to 500 wins. Variants (e.g. Suicide, Mirrors, Whiz) change bidding constraints only.
keyRules: Spades are always trump. Follow suit if able. Partnership bids are added; team must make combined bid to score. Nil bid: take zero tricks for bonus, or lose 100. No leading spades until spades are broken or hand is all spades. Winner of trick leads next. First to 500 points wins.

strategy.basic: In Suicide, if you have the Ace of Spades, you CANNOT bid Nil. Force your partner to bid Nil. In Mirrors, play aggressively with your Spades to make your bid, since everyone knows everyone's Spade count partially.
strategy.intermediate: Whiz Strategy: If you have 3 small Spades (2, 3, 4), bidding 3 is risky. Maybe bid Nil and hope to discard them on void suits? No, usually you must bid your Spade COUNT. So 3. You must take tricks with them.
strategy.advanced: Forcing Bags in Mirrors: Since bids are fixed, you can force opponents to take bags by leading suits they are long in but have low cards.
tips: Suicide is not for the faint of heart.
Mirrors removes bluffing about hand strength.

variations.name: Suicide
variations.description: One player of each partnership must bid Nil; the other bids normally.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes bidding constraint only; no engine constant overrides required.

variations.name: Mirrors
variations.description: Each player must bid exactly the number of spades in their hand.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes bidding constraint only; no engine constant overrides required.

variations.name: Whiz
variations.description: Players bid either Nil or the number of spades in hand.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes bidding constraint only; no engine constant overrides required.

scoring.description: Standard scoring unless specified (e.g., Suicide has higher penalties for failed Nil).
